title: Box a decorated cake for a customer without touching the frosting
instruction: Box the decorated cake for the customer: slide it into the cake box on its board, close the box and tuck the lid's tab in, without touching the frosting.
context: Protective retail food packaging without marring fragile surfaces is part of food preparation work (O*NET 35-2021.00, 'Package take-out foods or serve food to customers'; BLS May 2024 occupation total: 888,770 US jobs) and bakery counter production (51-3011.00 Bakers; occupation total: 231,890 US jobs), instantiated here on boxing a decorated whole cake. A 10 x 10 x 5 in lock-corner bakery carton (~146 g) slides on a smooth counter unless one hand braces it while the other slides the cake in by its 247.6 mm board rim (3.2 mm nominal clearance per side) without grazing piped borders or top rosettes; closing then requires folding the front panel up, bringing the window lid down, and pressing the lid while guiding its front tab inside the front panel. Closest accepted look-alike: TK-8A2A64 (crimp a foil pan rim onto a flat board lid); here a fragile piped cake is slid through a hinged carton throat and locked by tucking a paperboard tab.
setup: Two 6-DOF arms with parallel-jaw grippers sit at (0.00, +0.305) m and (0.00, -0.305) m along a smooth wipeable bakery counter (top z = 0.7475 m). Three loose 1:1 objects start on the counter: (1) a white 24-pt (0.6 mm) SBS paperboard 10 x 10 x 5 in lock-corner window bakery carton (BRP Box Shop #245, USD 29.36/10-pack or USD 117.42/100-pack at brpboxshop.com/245.html; Southern Champion Tray #23053 family; 254.0 x 254.0 x 127.0 mm inner cavity, ~0.146 kg estimated total mass, counter friction 0.52) centered at (0.3550, +0.1550) m angled +26 deg so its open throat faces toward the arms and counter. Per shipped template tasks/cake-box/fab/front_lifting_ear_template.svg, the two rear (+X) lock-corner tabs stay hooked and taped square (19 mm clear tape) while the two front (-X) 45 deg diagonal corner gussets are unhooked and slit flush along the side walls so the hinged 251.0 x 126.0 mm front panel unfolds flat onto the counter (-90 deg) and seats against the side walls at 0 deg; a declared two-ply 24-pt cardstock lifting ear (20.0 x 36.0 mm flange + 38.0 x 36.0 x 1.6 mm perpendicular ear, ~1.3 g, cut from fab/front_lifting_ear_template.svg and adhered with 19 mm double-sided tape at the +Y outer front corner, y_box = +130.4 mm, 3.4 mm outside the 254.0 mm throat) stands 39 mm off the counter for raising the flap, while the hinged 257.2 x 257.2 mm lid (174 x 174 mm clear window) starts open at 95 deg along the back wall with its tapered 35.0 mm front tuck tab at 45 deg outward; (2) a fabricated 247.6 mm OD x 4.8 mm thick (~0.055 kg, sliding friction 0.20) silver-foil-topped corrugated cake circle centered beside the box at (0.2253, -0.2175) m, made per shipped 1:1 template tasks/cake-box/fab/cake_board_template.svg by laminating two 10 in nominal Wilton corrugated white cake circles (MFR 191001569, USD 11.49/12-pack at WebstaurantStore #143191001569, ~254 mm stock OD, ~2.4 mm/ply) at 90 deg crossed flutes with PVA glue, wrapping the top face with 0.018 mm household silver aluminum foil, trimming to 247.6 +/- 0.5 mm OD with a 3.0 x 1.2 mm bottom kraft ski bevel (leaving 3.2 mm nominal wall clearance per side inside the 254.0 mm carton), and verifying OD, 4.8 +/- 0.4 mm thickness, and 55 +/- 6 g mass before use; and (3) a reusable cold room-temperature decorated cake stand-in adhered centered on the board with a royal-icing dab: an 8 x 3 in (203.2 x 76.2 mm) round polystyrene foam cake dummy (NY Cake, USD 7.99) covered in 2.4 mm pastel blush rolled fondant (208.0 mm body OD, 78.6 mm height) with hardened snow-white royal-icing bottom and top piped shell borders (108.5 mm max radius = 217.0 mm OD, leaving a 15.3 mm exposed silver board rim) and eight top swirl rosettes (93.5 mm peak height, 0.300 kg estimated mass, cake-to-board effective friction ~1.70). As on a bakery counter, the hand moves the cake into the box by pushing the exposed 15.3 mm silver board rim across the counter and flat unfolded front flap rather than lifting it.
scoring: Whole-trial sticky zero if at any step: any robot collision hull or any box panel comes within 1.0 mm of the cake's frosting (side fondant, bottom/top piped borders, top face, and rosettes, sampled <= 3.2 mm apart; bottom resting on board excluded); the cake tilts over 10.0 deg, slides over 10.0 mm, or lifts over 3.0 mm on its board; the board leaves the counter or box base by over 20.0 mm; or any box panel is forced past its crease stop (crushed). Otherwise, final state after 21 consecutive samples (1.0 s at 20 Hz) during which all six fingertip/pad points remain at least 80.0 mm from every box panel, the board, and the cake and all tracked 3D object points move under 1.0 mm all-pairs: 0.25 if the 247.6 mm cylindrical board's analytic 3D projection lies within the 254.0 x 254.0 mm inner base plus a 1.0 mm wall-contact/ruler allowance per side (projected half-extents <= 128.0 mm in X and Y, bottom face within 3.5 mm of the base floor); 0.5 if 0.25 holds and the front panel is within 5.0 deg of vertical; 0.75 if 0.5 holds and the window lid is within 5.0 deg of flat and within 3.0 mm of the 127.0 mm walls' tops all round; 1.0 if 0.75 holds and the lid's front tab is tucked inside the front panel with its free edge at least 10.0 mm behind the front panel's inner face (and at least 8.0 mm below its top edge); untouched start scores 0. Real trial: off-table over a tray, brush a thin film of food-grade unsweetened cocoa powder onto removable wipeable gripper-pad sleeves and the lid/tab underside before each trial (any brown mark on the white borders, rosettes, or pastel fondant, or any dent under a low-angle raking lamp, scores 0), record synchronised 30 fps overhead and side video (contact, drops, 1.0 s released stillness), check <= 1.0 mm board overhang past the 254 x 254 mm inner base lines, <= 3.0 mm lid-to-wall gap all round, >= 10.0 mm tab tuck depth, and >= 80.0 mm six-point hand clearance with a 1 mm steel ruler and 80 mm gauge block, then run the prospective retention check by lifting the closed carton 50 mm by its side walls and tilting 30 +/- 2 deg forward against a 30 deg wedge for 3 s to verify the front panel and tab stay tucked. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
fidelity: 0.6 mm SBS board uses 0.8-1.6 mm rigid panel proxies (1.6 mm walls) with estimated crease friction/hysteresis (0.008-0.085 N*m); the front tab is a hinged flap with a 0.001 N*m/rad spring and 14.5 mm root collider relief (fab/closure_cross_section.svg) so creasing tucks it behind the front wall. Board-in-base uses analytic 3D projection with a 1.0 mm wall/ruler allowance. Fondant/icing are rigid meshes with a <=3.2 mm contact latch (<1 mm); masses/frictions estimated; demo reads poses.
reset_notes: Cold room-temperature stand-in props only on a wipeable food-safe counter mat; wear clean nitrile gloves (and safety glasses when cutting templates). Before use, verify the fabricated two-ply silver-foil board (fab/cake_board_template.svg) with calipers (4.8 +/- 0.4 mm), a 1 mm steel ruler (247.6 +/- 0.5 mm OD), and a 1 g scale (55 +/- 6 g), and inspect the carton's taped rear corners, slit front gussets, and +Y lifting ear (fab/front_lifting_ear_template.svg); replace the carton if any crease is crushed. Off-table over a catch tray (never dusting loose powder near robot joints), lightly brush food-grade unsweetened cocoa powder onto removable nitrile/silicone fingertip sleeves and the lid/tab underside, then place the carton at (0.3550, +0.1550) m (yaw +26 deg) with front panel flat (-90 deg), lid open (~95 deg), and tab outward (~45 deg), and set the fondant/royal-icing dummy on its board at (0.2253, -0.2175) m handling only the 15.3 mm rim. Wipe the mat and pad sleeves with a damp cloth between trials; brush off or re-cover marked icing.
